title: Micron advanced U.S., Taiwan and global manufacturing capacity plans
canonical_summary: Micron's current capacity and capital-investment matter included large U.S. manufacturing commitments, Idaho and Taiwan expansion, new facilities, planned capital spending, site acquisition and related jobs and execution exposure.
known_event_summary: August 27-September 8, 2026 Micron capacity baseline: the company and public officials described more than $250 billion of U.S. manufacturing investment, Idaho/Taiwan expansion, new 2027-2028 facilities and capital spending above $25 billion.

facts.proposition: Micron maintained or raised a planned U.S. manufacturing investment of more than $250 billion through 2035.
Micron's U.S. expansion was described as creating tens of thousands of American jobs.
Micron is modernizing Taiwanese capacity for DRAM and HBM.
U.S. officials highlighted or praised Micron's approximately $250 billion domestic expansion commitment.
Micron warns that losing Taiwan production could materially adversely affect the company.
Micron Technology prioritizes fabrication capacity for advanced server DDR5, high-capacity solid-state storage, and specialized HBM3E modules.
Micron recently acquired a new Tongluo site to expand leading-edge memory production.
Micron has invested about $43.9 billion in Taiwan.
Micron's new production facilities were expected to come online from mid-2027 into 2028 or later.
Micron is constructing new production facilities to expand manufacturing capacity.
Micron planned capital spending exceeding $25 billion.
Micron was building additional memory-chip production capacity in Idaho.
